data.name: The Return Home Remastered
data.detailed_description:
A rabbit's house is being attacked by reptile menaces from another dimension. With advanced portal technology, they can achieve conquest of the entire planet! In retaliation, the rabbit has decided to gather carrots to exchange for weapons which may allow him to fend off this threat. Will he be able to succeed in his mission and return home?

Further details:


  • avoid the reptiles and gather the carrots
  • pass through enemy portals to close them
  • save the world by using the weapons, and then you can finally return to your home
  • first-person perspective immersion places you in the heat of the fight, use your fighting instinct to win the fight

Fun for any age, and a challenging game!

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows XP, Vista, 7, 8 or 10
  • Processador: 2.5 Ghz or faster processor (Intel) / 3.5 Ghz or faster processor (AMD)
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: 1 GB RAM / Widescreen
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 800 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: optional
  • Notas adicionais: These specifications might cause a slow loading time.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows Vista, 7, 8 or 10
  • Processador: 3 Ghz or faster processor (Intel) / 4 Ghz or faster processor (AMD)
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: 1,5 GB RAM / Widescreen
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 800 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: onboard
  • Notas adicionais: A Solid State Disk is recommended to speed up the loading time.

reviews.review:
The Return Home Remastered is a lighthearted first-person action game developed by AL-GAME and published by Displacement Studios. At its core, the game embraces a simple but entertaining premise: a peaceful rabbit's home has been invaded by hostile reptilian creatures emerging from mysterious dimensional portals. Rather than focusing on an elaborate narrative, the game delivers a straightforward adventure centered on exploration, combat, and progression. Its quirky concept immediately gives it a distinctive personality, creating an experience that feels more like a classic arcade shooter than a modern story-driven action title. While the plot is intentionally uncomplicated, it succeeds in providing enough motivation to keep players moving from one objective to the next.

Gameplay revolves around exploring each stage, gathering carrots scattered throughout the environments, purchasing stronger weapons, and eliminating waves of invading enemies before closing the portals that continue to fuel the attack. The carrot collection mechanic serves as both a reward for exploration and the game's primary currency, encouraging players to thoroughly search each level instead of simply rushing toward the objective. Unlocking new weapons gradually expands the combat options available, giving players a satisfying sense of progression despite the game's relatively modest scope. The controls are easy to learn, making the experience approachable for newcomers while still offering enough action to keep players engaged during firefights.

The remastered edition refreshes the presentation with improved visuals while maintaining the colorful and playful aesthetic of the original release. Environments are bright and easy to navigate, complementing the game's humorous premise rather than attempting to deliver realistic graphics. Character models and enemy designs reinforce the whimsical atmosphere, allowing the unusual conflict between an armed rabbit and invading reptiles to feel surprisingly cohesive. Although the visual upgrades help modernize the experience, the game remains clearly rooted in its independent origins, with modest production values that prioritize smooth performance and accessibility over cutting-edge graphical effects.

Combat provides the game's primary source of entertainment through steady action and a growing arsenal of weapons. Enemies appear frequently enough to maintain a consistent pace, and destroying portals creates satisfying moments of accomplishment as players slowly reclaim each area from the invasion. However, the overall gameplay loop remains largely unchanged throughout the adventure. Missions repeatedly ask players to collect resources, defeat enemies, and eliminate portals, which can eventually make the experience feel repetitive during extended sessions. Likewise, enemy behavior lacks significant variety, reducing the strategic depth that could have made later encounters more engaging.

Despite these limitations, The Return Home Remastered succeeds by understanding its own ambitions. It does not attempt to compete with large-scale shooters packed with cinematic storytelling or complex progression systems. Instead, it offers a compact and accessible action experience that can be enjoyed in shorter play sessions. Features such as Steam Cloud support, Trading Cards, Family Sharing, and full English voice acting further enhance the overall package, while the game's modest hardware requirements allow it to run comfortably on a wide range of PCs. Players looking for an easy-to-pick-up indie shooter with an unusual premise will likely appreciate its straightforward design philosophy.

Ultimately, The Return Home Remastered is a charming independent action game that delivers enjoyable first-person shooting without unnecessary complexity. Its humorous premise, accessible gameplay, satisfying weapon progression, and relaxed pacing make it a pleasant experience for players seeking casual entertainment. Although repetitive objectives, limited enemy variety, and relatively simple presentation prevent it from reaching the heights of more ambitious shooters, the game remains an enjoyable example of an indie project that embraces creativity over scale. For players who appreciate quirky concepts and arcade-inspired gameplay, it offers enough charm and action to justify the journey back home.

Rating: 5/10
